sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: New technology-enabled roles should help workers progress through and beyond the Progressive Wage Model.

sections.label: Redesigning transport roles for disabilities
sections.summary: As transport jobs become digital and less physical, MOT should work with SG Enable, employers and unions to redesign roles for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As more transport jobs become digital, remote-enabled and less physically demanding, new opportunities become possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope MOT can work together with SG Enable, employers and unions to redesign suitable roles so that more persons with disabilities can participate meaningfully in our transport sector.

sections.label: Singapore transshipment and container ports
sections.summary: Singapore is now the world's busiest transshipment port and the second busiest container port.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Singapore is now the busiest transshipment port in the world, and the second busiest container port.

sections.label: Singapore maritime hub rankings
sections.summary: Singapore is the world's largest bunkering hub, fourth largest ship registry by tonnage, and second most preferred arbitration seat globally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Over time, we have grown into major hubs for many of these parallel industries as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We are the world's largest bunkering hub, accounting for about 40% of global bunker sales.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Our ship registry is the fourth largest in the world by tonnage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: When trade disputes arise, and take it from a lawyer, they always do, Singapore is a globally recognised hub for maritime law and dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We are actually the world's second most preferred arbitration seat globally, second only to London, and number one in Asia.

sections.label: Intangible qualities underpinning Singapore's survival
sections.summary: Singapore's survival depends on tending the intangible qualities underpinning its system, not just investing in technology and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Because for Singapore, these are the very conditions for our survival.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, when we ask how do we reinforce Singapore's position as a maritime hub, the real question is not whether to keep investing in future technology like AI or next generation infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The real question is whether we continue tending to the intangible qualities that underpin our system and make us exceptional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: That, Sir, will determine if we can continue to earn our place in the world.

sections.label: Singapore as confident trade decision hub
sections.summary: Singapore should aspire to become the place where trade decisions are made with confidence, not only to move trade efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore should therefore aspire not only to move trade efficiently, but to become the place where those decisions are made with confidence.

sections.label: Trust and transport investments
sections.summary: Trust is part of Singapore's economic infrastructure, making investments in Tuas Port and Changi T5 important for Singapore's relevance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Trust has become part of Singapore's economic infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That is why investments in Tuas Port and Changi T5 are so important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They are investments in Singapore's relevance for the next generation.

sections.label: Singapore as decision-making place
sections.summary: Singapore must become the place where the world's most important transport and supply chain decisions are made with confidence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In a world that is becoming more uncertain, Singapore must become the place where the world's most important transport and supply chain decisions are made with confidence.

sections.label: Workforce transformation investments questioned
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes investments in workforce transformation and asks how billions in T5, Tuas Port and transport technologies will translate into better jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Their concern is whether they will be equipped to succeed in this new environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Government' continued investments in workforce transformation like the OneAviation Manpower Fund and various SkillsFuture initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But my question to the Minister is this: as we invest billions in T5, Tuas Port and new transport technologies, how will the Ministry ensure these investments translate into better jobs, stronger career progression and higher value opportunities for Singaporeans?

sections.label: Long-term transport nerve centre strategy
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry has a long-term strategy to position Singapore as the region's nerve centre for transport and supply chain management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: My question to the Minister is this: beyond strengthening Singapore's physical connectivity, does the Ministry have a long-term strategy to position Singapore as the region's nerve centre for transport and supply chain management?

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: How will MOT work with other agencies and our tripartite partners to anchor these higher-value activities and the good jobs they create in Singapore?

sections.label: Integrated National Transport Talent Strategy
sections.summary: The speaker proposes an integrated National Transport Talent Strategy to ensure Singaporeans take on high-value jobs emerging across the transport sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: As we strengthen our position as a global transport hub, we should consider a more integrated National Transport Talent Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Such a strategy could bring together Government agencies, industries, our IHLs and SkillsFuture partners to regularly identify emerging skills, develop future-ready curricula, expand internships and overseas industrial attachments to ensure that Singaporeans are well positioned to take on the high-value jobs that will emerge across our transport sector.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The best way to anchor good jobs is not simply to attract investment, but to ensure that our Singaporeans possess capabilities that investors cannot easily find elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Our task is not to predict every technological change, but to ensure that Singaporeans have the adaptability and the opportunities to keep learning throughout their careers.

sections.label: Transport's economic contribution
sections.summary: Transport contributes about a-tenth of GDP and 7% of jobs, held by Singaporeans moving people and goods by air, land and sea.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Transport is one of the largest economic sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It contributes about a-tenth of our GDP and 7% of our jobs – good, steady, high-paying jobs, held by Singaporeans who keep people and goods moving, by air, land and sea, every hour, every day.

sections.label: Transport sector directions
sections.summary: At Committee of Supply, three directions were set for the transport sector: globally-oriented, future-focused and people-centric.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: At this year's Committee of Supply, I set out three directions for our transport sector: to be globally-oriented, future-focused and people-centric.

sections.label: Singapore IMO ICAO elections
sections.summary: In last year's IMO and ICAO Council elections, Singapore received the highest number of votes in its category.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: In the Council elections for the IMO and for the ICAO last year, Singapore received the highest number of votes in our category.

sections.label: Singapore global transport agreements
sections.summary: Singapore's agreements worldwide help explain flights to over 170 cities and seaport connections to more than 600 locations.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Singapore has built a web of agreements around the world – Air Services Agreements, Green and Digital Shipping Corridors, and many more.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: They help explain why our airport has flights to over 170 cities today and our seaports have connections to more than 600 other locations.

sections.label: Global Competitiveness Committee conclusion
sections.summary: The Global Competitiveness Committee concluded Singapore must further strengthen its role as a connected global hub.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: The Global Competitiveness Committee, which I co-chaired with Senior Minister of State Low Yen Ling, concluded that Singapore must further strengthen our role as a connected global hub.

sections.label: Transport technology funding projects
sections.summary: Eight hundred million is more than double the last five years' funding, for projects like automated depots, AI air traffic management and smart port networks.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Eight hundred million is more than double the funding over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For instance, imagine a fully automated MRT depot that maintains and repairs our trains more efficiently, or an AI-enabled air traffic management system that increases our regional airspace capacity to accommodate the needs of all the airports around us, or a smart port network that makes decisions with shipping lines on how to shift containers on a real-time basis, using tools like digital twins, which Mr Jackson Lam and Ms Tin both spoke about.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: If these projects succeed in the next decade, Singapore will still remain as one of the world's major transport and logistics hubs, but it will look completely different.

sections.label: T5 and Tuas Port capacity
sections.summary: T5 will raise Changi's capacity by more than 50%, and Tuas Port will go from 45 million to 65 million TEUs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: T5 will raise Changi's capacity by more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Tuas Port will bring us from 45 million TEUs today to 65 million TEUs in the future.

sections.label: Taxi and private-hire driver numbers
sections.summary: Singapore has over 70,000 taxi and private-hire drivers, while all AVs worldwide number around 7,000 cars.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Today, there are over 70,000 taxi and private-hire drivers in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Even if I gathered every AV around the world today and moved them all to Singapore, that would only be around 7,000 cars – or less than 10% of our total taxi and private-hire car population.

sections.label: Cleaner-energy vehicle registrations and charging points
sections.summary: From 2030 all new car and taxi registrations will be cleaner-energy models, with 60,000 charging points targeted by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: From 2030, all new car and taxi registrations will be cleaner-energy models, supporting Singapore's broader goal for all vehicles to run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government is also working towards deploying 60,000 charging points island-wide by 2030.

sections.label: Heavy vehicle zero emissions incentives
sections.summary: From January 2026 a $40,000 incentive applies per newly registered zero-tailpipe-emissions heavy vehicle, with charger grants capped at $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: From January 2026, the Heavy Vehicle Zero Emissions Scheme provides a $40,000 incentive for each newly registered zero-tailpipe-emissions heavy goods vehicle or bus above 3.5 tonnes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Electric Heavy Vehicle Charger Grant also co-funds up to 50% of charger installation costs, capped at $30,000 per charger for the first 500 chargers.

sections.label: Singapore-Kuala Lumpur high-speed rail distance
sections.summary: The roughly 350 kilometre Singapore-Kuala Lumpur distance is considered a sweet spot for high-speed rail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At about 350 kilometres in distance between Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, this is a sweet spot for high-speed rail, where it is widely considered to be “too far to drive conveniently and too short to fly”.

sections.label: High-speed rail revival discussions
sections.summary: No decision has been reached on reviving the HSR, and Singapore remains open to a commercially viable proposal from Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: While Malaysia explored the possibility of reviving the HSR in 2023 under a different delivery model, no decision has since been reached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government has consistently maintained that it remains open to future discussions should Malaysia bring forward a commercially viable proposal that serves the interests of both countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Of course, the challenges that led to the project's cancellation remain significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: These include the substantial capital costs, questions surrounding financing and ownership structures, cross-border governance arrangements, commercial risk allocation and the need for sustained political commitment from both sides.

sections.label: SBS Transit predictive maintenance solutions
sections.summary: SBS Transit envisioned predictive AI-enabled maintenance across bus and rail operations, consulting workers through NTUC's initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: To enhance workplace safety and raise productivity, SBS Transit envisioned a predictive AI-enabled maintenance solutions across its bus and rail maintenance operations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Working closely with NTUC through the NTUC Company Training Committee initiative, SBS Transit consulted widely with workers before implementing a suite of predictive maintenance solutions from tyre and track inspections to facility management in its depots and interchanges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Through its Diagnostic Expert Scheme, workers could move into higher-value maintenance work with progressive career pathways, enhanced livelihoods and safer workplaces.

sections.label: P2P drivers stop earning
sections.summary: P2P drivers stop earning the moment they stop driving, unlike salaried employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Unlike salaried employees, P2P drivers stop earning the moment they stop driving.

sections.label: AI transition motion and tripartite work
sections.summary: The House unanimously passed the AI transition motion, and the Government is urged to work with NTUC, unions and the Tripartite Jobs Council on evolving jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: This House unanimously passed the Motion on "An AI Transition with No Jobless Growth" in May.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: I encourage and urge the Government to continue working closely with NTUC, our unions and our Tripartite Jobs Council to identify how jobs are evolving, expand AI Ready SG to equip more workers with AI capabilities and encourage more companies to leverage our Company Training Committee grants to support job redesign and workforce transformation across the entire transport sector.

sections.label: EV Technical Specialists Skills Pathway
sections.summary: The recently launched Skills Pathway for EV Technical Specialists is an encouraging step in this direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The recently launched Skills Pathway for EV Technical Specialists is an encouraging step in this direction.

sections.label: Sector-level report card proposal
sections.summary: One possibility is a sector-level report card in Industry Transformation Maps tracking creation, quality and the 3Ws of jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: One possibility is a sector-level report card within our Industry Transformation Maps that tracks whether new and redesigned jobs are being created, whether these jobs are of good quality and whether they deliver what NTUC calls the "3Ws" – better wages, better welfare and better work prospects.

sections.label: Labour Movement seat at table
sections.summary: The Labour Movement must keep a seat at the table on deployment, liability, regulatory frameworks and AV industry local jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: This is a nascent space and it is important that the Labour Movement continues to have a seat at the table.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We will continue speaking up for workers on deployment concerns, liability and regulatory frameworks, and more importantly, how the AV industry can create good local jobs and build Singaporean capabilities.

sections.label: Redesigning jobs for transport workers
sections.summary: Redesigning jobs early, with proper transition arrangements and drivers at the centre, lets technology bring new skills, roles and a better future.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: As long as we redesign jobs for our drivers early, put proper transition arrangements in place and keep our drivers at the centre of that transition, technology can bring them new skills, new roles and a better future. : Throughout my engagements, one question stayed with me: "Where do I fit in the future of transport?" Our responsibility is to ensure that every transport worker has an answer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: A pathway to better skills, better jobs and better livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: We may not be able to preserve every job exactly as it exists today, but we must preserve livelihoods and create pathways to the next good job.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: If we get this right, Singapore will not only remain as the world's leading transport hub, we will become something even more important – a transport hub where innovation advances together with workers, and where progress is measured not only by how far technology takes us, but by how far it brings our people along.

sections.label: Tuas Port and T5 capacity

sentences.text: Tuas Port will handle 65 million containers a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: T5 will lift Changi towards 140 million passengers.

sections.label: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, signed last year, opens a new chapter for both sides of the Causeway.

sections.label: Changi check-in in Johor

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, open Changi check-in and baggage handling in Johor itself so a traveller can begin a Changi journey from Johor Bahru.

sections.label: National Crisis Logistics Compact proposal
sections.summary: The Government is urged to set up a National Crisis Logistics Compact with MOT, MTI, MFA, Defence and industry partners, with year-one measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If our autonomy is compromised, or even seems to be, we lose the confidence that brings people here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I would therefore urge the Government to set up a National Crisis Logistics Compact, bringing MOT, MTI, MFA, the Ministry of Defence and major industry partners into one framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In year one, it should stress-test our five most critical supply chains, run a whole-of-nation logistics exercise modelled after Exercise Northstar, publish a Hub Resilience Statement and establish a standing industry council for crisis coordination.

sections.label: Marine fuel and undersea cables
sections.summary: A country supplying close to a fifth of the world's marine fuel should help write standards and seek stronger international protection for undersea cables and navigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A country that supplies close to a fifth of the world's marine fuel, 56.77 million tonnes last year, should be helping write those standards, not receiving them second-hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Stronger international protection for undersea cables, for freedom of navigation through chokepoints, and for the infrastructure the digital economy sits on.

sections.label: Singapore as open economy
sections.summary: Singapore should keep faith, connecting to the world, anchoring enterprise, creating jobs and keeping supplies flowing reliably and affordably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A hundred years from now, when our great grandchildren ask what sort of country this was, I want them to be able to say what merchants once said of the Hanseatic cities: they knew what to expect of Singapore; and Singapore kept faith.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It connects Singapore to the world, anchors enterprise, creates good jobs and secures our future as an open economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For Singaporeans, this means in a very practical ways: efficient port, airport, logistics networks help keep food, medicine, household goods and business inputs flowing reliably and affordably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They also strengthen national resilience in a crisis: strong aviation, maritime and logistics links give Singapore more options to secure essential supplies and keep trade routes open.

sentences.text: For example, the Sea Transport Industry Digital Plan provides a clear roadmap to guide maritime SMEs in adopting digital solutions at each stage of their growth while building the necessary skills.

sentences.text: Under the MPA-Singapore Polytechnic Maritime SME Digital Adoption Pilot Programme, SMEs gain knowledge on digital technologies and acquire practical experience in applying automation and data analytics to their operations directly.

sections.label: Transport sector youth support

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Through scholarships, work attachments and mentorship programmes, we will continue to help young Singaporeans gain skills and build meaningful careers in the transport sector.

sentences.text: Last July, I launched the $200 million OneAviation Manpower Fund to support employers, unions and workers.

sections.summary: A manpower transition package with tripartite partners aims to help taxi and private hire car drivers keep up with industry developments and explore new careers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Together with our tripartite partners, we have put together a manpower transition package to empower our taxi and private hire car drivers to stay ahead of industry developments and to explore new career options with confidence.

sections.label: Driver training incentive scheme
sections.summary: From January 2027, a pilot training incentive scheme will give eligible drivers $20 per hour for over 2,000 curated courses, capped at 80 hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Second, we will pilot a new training incentive scheme from January 2027, focusing on short-form courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: They also incur other costs such as car rental expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Hence, under this scheme, eligible drivers will get a training incentive of $20 per hour for attending any of over 2,000 curated SWDA-supported courses, up to a cap of 80 hours of training.

sections.label: Manpower Transition Package for drivers
sections.summary: A Manpower Transition Package will support taxi and private-hire drivers through career transition, skills training and career guidance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: At the same time, our tripartite partners are actively working together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will be introducing a Manpower Transition Package to support taxi and private-hire drivers through career transition, skills training and career guidance.

sections.label: Changi East Development and T5
sections.summary: The Changi East Development, including T5, positions Changi Airport for the future of air travel, anchoring jobs and the economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Changi East Development, including T5, positions Changi Airport for the future of air travel, anchoring good jobs and a significant part of our economy.

sections.label: Sustainable aviation fuel uplift goal
sections.summary: The goal is a 1% sustainable aviation fuel uplift, rising to 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and fuel availability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our goal is to start with a 1% sustainability aviation fuel uplift, rising to 3% to 5% by 2030, subject to global developments and the wider availability of sustainability aviation fuel.

sections.label: Electric heavy vehicle registrations rise
sections.summary: With adoption and charger incentives, electric heavy vehicle registrations rose from under 1% last year to around 20% as of May this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With the adoption and charger incentives for heavy vehicles, registrations of electric heavy vehicles rose from less than 1% of all heavy vehicle registrations last year to around 20% as of May this year.

sections.label: Electric and hybrid-electric aircraft technology
sections.summary: Electric and hybrid-electric aircraft are emerging but in the short term can only complement sustainable aviation fuel-powered aircraft, as the technology may take time to commercialise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Electric and hybrid-electric aircraft is an emerging technology but in the short term, they can only complement aircrafts powered by sustainable aviation fuel as hybrid-electric aircraft technology may take time to commercialise and are not yet suitable for deployment.

sections.label: Drones, innovation and economic competitiveness
sections.summary: Drones can improve productivity and worker safety; Singapore is studying their deployment and will support responsible innovation through trials, testbeds and regulatory refinement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Many of these use cases improve productivity and worker safety, allowing workers to focus on tasks that call for human judgement and expertise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are carefully studying how drones can be deployed while being mindful of Singapore's dense urban environment, complex airspace and security needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will continue to support responsible innovation through trials, testbeds and regulatory refinement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Our best chance at delivering a good life for our people is to strengthen Singapore’s long-term economic competitiveness and anchor good jobs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This can be achieved through international cooperation, appropriate use of frontier technologies and establishing world-class infrastructure to reinforce our position as a globally connected aviation, maritime and logistics hub.

sections.label: Thanks to three ministers
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Minister Jeffrey Siow, Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling and Minister of State Baey Yam Keng for their receptiveness and positive responses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: I am also especially appreciative of the receptiveness and positive responses from Minister Jeffrey Siow, Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling and Minister of State Baey Yam Keng.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We are very excited that some of our suggestions will be accepted by the Ministry and we are also very heartened by the efforts made past and present.

sections.label: Singapore asserting independence confidently
sections.summary: Singapore can assert its independence with confidence when it builds strong capabilities, has connection options and deepens international cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: When Singapore builds strong capabilities of our own, when we have options to who we connect with and when we deepen international cooperation so that other countries come to share a genuine stake in our shared success, Singapore will be able to assert our independence with confidence.

sections.label: Exporting Singapore model, jobs
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore is exporting its model of trust, and that speakers insisted this must translate into jobs for Singaporean workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We are, in essence, exporting the Singapore model, our special brand of trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: And on our people, nearly every speaker insisted that none of this matters unless it translates into good, better and more inclusive jobs for Singaporean workers with real training pathways and real protection for those whose roles will change.

sections.label: Agreement on Singapore's direction
sections.summary: The passage states public transport and global connectivity are not competing priorities, and that the House agrees on Singapore's direction across party lines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Attending to the everyday public transport issues and building for Singapore's global connectivity and future are not competing priorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We agree that the world has grown more uncertain and that Singapore's independence must be built, not assumed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We agree that technology should make us harder to replace, not just harder to keep pace with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: We agree that our infrastructure, physical and digital, poured in concrete and written in code, must be built as one so that it can keep pace with a future that will wait for no one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: And we agree that our people must remain at the centre of everything we build.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: When a House this diverse agrees completely on the big one, that is not a coincidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: It is Singapore's direction spoken with one voice across party lines and with that, thank you all.
